content: Clarithromycin (DrugBank DB01211) is a macrolide antibiotic that acts by inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis by binding to the 50S ribosomal subunit. It is a strong inhibitor of CYP3A4 and a moderate inhibitor of CYP1A2. Clarithromycin also inhibits P-glycoprotein (P-gp), increasing the bioavailability of P-gp substrates such as digoxin, colchicine, and dabigatran. The drug has 341 known drug interactions in DrugBank. Major interactions include: statins (rhabdomyolysis risk), warfarin (bleeding risk via CYP3A4 inhibition), ergot alkaloids (ergotism), benzodiazepines (excessive sedation), carbamazepine (toxicity), theophylline (toxicity), and QT-prolonging agents (arrhythmia risk). Clarithromycin is hepatically metabolized to 14-hydroxyclarithromycin, which also has antimicrobial activity. Renal dose adjustment is required when CrCl is less than 30 mL/min.
